nice_guideline_used: CG126 / NG185 (Ischemic heart disease) and NG136 (Hypertension)

medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends amlodipine as first‑line antihypertensive in patients ≥55 y or as part of combination therapy
NICE NG136 includes thiazide‑type diuretics as part of step‑3 triple therapy for hypertension

medications.purpose: Hypertension and cardioprotection in coronary artery disease
medications.nice_justification: CG126/NG185 recommends ACE‑I for all IHD patients; NG136 lists ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension

medications.dose: 500 mg extended‑release oral tablet once daily
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin as first‑line therapy for T2DM

medications.dose: 75 mg oral tablet once daily (enteric‑coated if GI risk)
medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of cardiovascular events in established CAD
medications.nice_justification: CG126/NG185: antiplatelet therapy (aspirin 75 mg) is lifelong for all patients with confirmed IHD

medications.dose: 80 mg oral tablet once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: LDL‑C reduction to achieve ≥40 % non‑HDL‑C reduction or LDL‑C <1.8 mmol/L in CAD
medications.nice_justification: CG126/NG185: high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) is first‑line for all patients with IHD regardless of baseline cholesterol

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma concentrations (~1.5‑fold) raising risk of myopathy
interactions_checked.action: Monitor CK and symptoms of myopathy; no dose reduction required unless toxicity occurs

interactions_checked.interaction: Thiazides may modestly increase statin levels
interactions_checked.action: Routine monitoring of CK; no routine dose change

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined ACE‑I and thiazide can increase serum potassium
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium and renal function within 2 weeks of initiation/adjustment, then annually

contraindications.reason: Negative inotrope; contraindicated in patients with CAD and potential heart failure
contraindications.alternative: Amlodipine (already prescribed) or other CCB without negative inotropic effect

contraindications.reason: Negative inotrope; contraindicated in CAD with possible LV dysfunction
Fluid retention and risk of heart failure; patient has CAD and hypertension
contraindications.alternative: Continue metformin; consider SGLT2 inhibitor if glucose control needed

contraindications.reason: Dual RAAS blockade increases renal injury risk; patient already on ACE‑I
contraindications.alternative: Do not add ARB unless ACE‑I intolerant

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed >30 mL/min/1.73 m²; will obtain serum creatinine/eGFR before starting high‑intensity statin and repeat after 2 weeks.
Baseline liver function tests (ALT/AST, bilirubin) not available – assumed normal; will check before initiating atorvastatin.
Baseline CK not available – will obtain before statin start to detect any underlying myopathy.
Allergy status unknown – will confirm no aspirin or statin intolerance before prescribing.
Smoking status not recorded – will assess and offer cessation support if patient smokes.
Blood pressure target not documented – will verify that current regimen achieves <140/90 mmHg (or <130/80 mmHg if diabetic).
treatment_summary: The patient with established atherosclerotic coronary artery disease should receive lifelong aspirin 75 mg and high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg for secondary prevention, in addition to their existing antihypertensive regimen (lisinopril, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide) and metformin for diabetes. Interactions are modest and manageable with routine monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, CK and liver enzymes. No contraindicated agents are added, and assumptions regarding renal and hepatic function, CK, and smoking status are noted for verification.
